newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols static, waiting on the U.S..
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols static, waiting on the U.S..

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options on LIFFE was at a standstill and volume skimpy ahead of a clutch of U.S. data and a Federal Reserve policy meeting, traders said.
"It's a quiet morning," said a broker at a French brokerage in London. "We've got NAPM this afternoon and payrolls on Thursday. As the week progresses it should get better."

He quoted implied volatility of August options at around 5.1/5.1 percent, September at 5.18/5.35 percent, October at 5.33/5.45 and December at 5.41/5.54 percent. All were broadly unchanged on Monday's close, he said.
At 1000 GMT, September Bund futures were quoted at 101.45, down four basis points from Monday's pit settlement.
Mourad Amellel, a trader at Transoptions Finance in London, said a wide strangle in December options was one feature of trade so far.
A British bank sold 300 lots each of 94.50 and 95.50 puts and 300 lots each of the 105.50 and 106.00 calls at volatility of around 5.14 percent, he said.
In the front month August options, LIFFE data show 102.50 calls busy with 1,865 lots traded and the 100.50 puts trading volume of 2,035 lots. September 102.00 calls attracted volume of 1,500 lots.
"They're all waiting on the U.S.," said Amellel.
U.S. data this afternoon includes the June survey from the National Association of Purchasing Management at 1400 GMT, and May construction spending and May leading indicators, also at 1400 GMT.
Data from Chicago Purchasing Managers spooked the market on Monday after the index showed a rise to 61.5 in June from 56.8 percent in the previous month.

A two-day Federal Open Market Committee meeting begins on Tuesday while June payrolls were due on Thursday ahead of the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
